item.title: Critical Infrastructure Protection: Further Action Needed to Enhance Cybersecurity of the Food and Agriculture Sector
item.description:
What GAO Found
Increased use of technologies in the food and agriculture sector has made the sector more vulnerable to cybersecurity incidents, such as ransomware attacks. For example, a 2021 ransomware attack on a global meat processing company shut down some of the world’s largest slaughterhouses and caused a shortage in meat supplies in the U.S. and other countries.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and the Department of Health and Human Services’ Food and Drug Administration (FDA), as agencies primarily responsible for federal efforts to enhance the sector’s cybersecurity, have taken a number of actions to improve the cybersecurity of the sector, but key steps remain. The agencies met most of the cyber-related aspects of the16 requirements under the six categories in the Fiscal Year 2021 National Defense Authorization Act, such as sector coordination, but only partially met or did not meet five requirements in the areas of information sharing and emergency preparedness aimed at better mitigating cybersecurity risks and attacks in the sector.
Extent to Which Sector Risk Management Agencies Have Met Requirements for Food and Agriculture Sector Cybersecurity
Both agencies reported that a lack of resources and staffing hindered their ability to meet all the requirements. By assessing whether there are opportunities to reprioritize or if there is a need for additional resources, the agencies would be better positioned to provide cybersecurity-related assistance and resources to the sector and help mitigate potential disruption of the food supply chain, which could lead to significant economic and environmental impacts.
In addition, selected private sector organizations reported actions to improve the cybersecurity of the sector, including sharing cyber alerts and distributing guidance to their members. The organizations also shared their views on opportunities and challenges to improve cybersecurity in the sector, including an increased need for collaboration between federal agencies and sector members.
Why GAO Did This Study
The food and agriculture sector is one of the nation’s 16 critical infrastructure sectors and is essential to the nation’s health, security, and economy. The sector is reliant on information technology to produce, process, and deliver products, and faces increasing cybersecurity-related risks. Cyberattacks could result in unsafe food and could erode public trust and faith in the food supply.
In this report, GAO (1) describes the potential cybersecurity risks to the sector; (2) evaluates the extent to which responsible federal agencies have taken actions to improve the cybersecurity of the sector; and (3) describes selected private sector organizations’ actions and views to improve the cybersecurity of the sector.
GAO summarized publicly available information on cyberattacks impacting the sector. GAO analyzed actions taken by USDA and FDA to improve the cybersecurity of the sector and compared them to the 16 requirements in the Fiscal Year 2021 National Defense Authorization Act. GAO interviewed relevant federal officials and a nongeneralizable sample of six private sector organizations comprising a cross section of the sector.
